title: LessonPlanner: Assisting Novice Teachers to Prepare Pedagogy-Driven Lesson Plans with Large Language Models
venue: The 37th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology (UIST '24)
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether a large-language-model-based planning tool can help novice teachers create better lesson plans with less effort. The authors focus on a common challenge in teaching preparation: novice teachers often struggle to design pedagogically sound lesson plans, choose effective teaching strategies, and locate or adapt suitable instructional materials. The paper also asks what kinds of support teachers need when using LLMs for lesson planning, and whether a specialized interface can outperform a general-purpose ChatGPT interface.

To address this, the authors first conducted a formative qualitative study with six novice teachers or teaching assistants to identify needs and design requirements. Based on these findings, they built LessonPlanner, a web application powered by GPT-4 that structures lesson planning around Gagne's Nine Events of Instruction and supports goal generation using Bloom's Taxonomy. The system provides an outline-generation workflow, block-based lesson plan editing, preset prompts for common pedagogical actions, contextual generation of teaching materials and activities, and flexible options for revising, regenerating, or querying content.

The empirical evaluation combined quantitative and qualitative methods. A within-subjects study with 12 university students acting as novice teachers compared LessonPlanner against a baseline condition using the ChatGPT web app plus search and a markdown editor. Participants prepared 90-minute lesson plans for familiar data structures topics. The paper reports that LessonPlanner significantly improved the quality of the resulting lesson plans and reduced users' workload relative to the baseline. The researchers also conducted expert think-aloud interviews with six teachers from different educational levels and subjects, who generally found the system useful for organizing lesson outlines, suggesting teaching strategies, and generating meaningful teaching resources.

Overall, the paper concludes that a pedagogy-guided, purpose-built LLM interface can support lesson planning more effectively than a generic chatbot interface, particularly for novice teachers. At the same time, the findings highlight concerns about the trustworthiness, subject-specific quality, and accuracy of generated content, suggesting that human oversight remains necessary. The authors argue for future educational LLM systems that combine strong pedagogical scaffolding with flexible user control.

identified_tools.name: LessonPlanner
identified_tools.description: A web-based lesson planning system powered by an OpenAI GPT-4 family model that helps teachers generate pedagogy-driven lesson goals, outlines, teaching materials, and activity suggestions structured around Gagne’s Nine Events of Instruction.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as an interactive lesson-planning assistant for novice teachers preparing 90-minute lesson plans; compared against the baseline ChatGPT web interface in a within-subjects study, with additional expert interviews on usefulness and usability.

findings.finding_summary: In a within-subjects study, LessonPlanner significantly improved the quality of outcome lesson plans and reduced users’ workload compared with the baseline ChatGPT interface. The paper reports participant sample size N=12 for the comparative study, but the excerpt does not provide the exact effect sizes, confidence intervals, or per-measure test statistics.
findings.measure: Lesson plan quality ratings and workload during lesson preparation versus baseline ChatGPT

findings.finding_summary: Expert interviews indicated that LessonPlanner was useful for lesson planning because it provided a well-organized outline and inspiring content, and helped suggest effective teaching strategies and meaningful educational resources. The expert evaluation involved N=6 teachers, but no quantitative effect sizes were reported in the excerpt.
findings.measure: Expert perceptions of usefulness for lesson planning, teaching strategy suggestion, and resource support

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI’s general-purpose LLM chatbot interface used for free-form prompting and content generation.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the baseline interface for lesson planning, against which LessonPlanner was compared in the within-subjects study.

findings.finding_summary: Compared with LessonPlanner, the baseline ChatGPT interface produced lower-quality lesson plans and higher workload in the within-subjects comparison. The study sample was N=12, but the excerpt does not report exact baseline scores, effect sizes, or confidence intervals.
findings.measure: Comparative lesson plan quality and workload in lesson preparation

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical mixed-methods paper with a within-subjects comparative user study (N=12) and expert interviews (N=6), but the excerpt does not provide full statistical details or rigorous causal education outcome evidence such as RCT/QED student learning impacts.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports significant improvements in lesson plan quality and workload for LessonPlanner versus ChatGPT, suggesting positive operational impact, but effect sizes and detailed outcome magnitudes are not reported in the excerpt, so impact remains unclear in magnitude.
